category.name: Track Changes
category.preferred_workflow: Create a Document, call Document.StartTrackRevisions with author and date, perform the required edits using DocumentBuilder, call Document.StopTrackRevisions, examine Document.Revisions (or its Groups) to verify the expected revision types, apply AcceptAllRevisions, RejectAllRevisions, or individual Revision.Accept/Reject as needed, and finally save the document to the requested format.

strict_api_bans: Do not reference members that are not present in Aspose.Words 26.11.0.
Do not import or use fictitious namespaces or classes.
Do not call revision-related methods that are not part of the official API surface.
canonical_patterns: Use Document.StartTrackRevisions and Document.StopTrackRevisions to control revision capture.
Inspect revisions through Document.Revisions and, when needed, group information via RevisionCollection.Groups.
Accept or reject revisions with Revision.Accept, Revision.Reject, Document.AcceptAllRevisions, or Document.RejectAllRevisions.
Use the HasRevisions property to decide whether additional actions such as watermark insertion are required.
nullable_warning_prevention: Create any source files, images, or folders in the sample code before loading them.
Validate that a document was successfully loaded before accessing its nodes.
Always call Document.Save after the requested modifications to guarantee output existence.

common_failure_patterns.symptom: Compilation fails because types such as RevisionGroups, RevisionDate, or RevisionNode are not found.
common_failure_patterns.cause: The code references revision members that were never implemented in the selected Aspose.Words version.
common_failure_patterns.fix: Replace the nonexistent members with the documented Revision, RevisionCollection, and RevisionType APIs.
common_failure_patterns.prevention: Consult the official Aspose.Words 26.11.0 reference before using any revision-related type or property.

common_failure_patterns.symptom: Compilation errors indicate that methods like StartTrackRevisions or StopTrackRevisions are missing on DocumentBuilder.
common_failure_patterns.cause: Revision tracking methods were called on DocumentBuilder instead of the Document instance.
common_failure_patterns.fix: Invoke StartTrackRevisions and StopTrackRevisions on the Document object, not on DocumentBuilder.
common_failure_patterns.prevention: Remember that tracking is a document-level feature; only Document exposes the tracking methods.

common_failure_patterns.symptom: Runtime checks report that zero or an unexpected number of revisions were produced.
common_failure_patterns.cause: Edits were performed while tracking was disabled or before StartTrackRevisions was called.
common_failure_patterns.fix: Enable tracking before making any modifications and ensure StopTrackRevisions is called only after the edits are complete.
common_failure_patterns.prevention: Structure the code so that all tracked edits occur between StartTrackRevisions and StopTrackRevisions.

common_failure_patterns.symptom: Runtime exception occurs when a revision is accepted or rejected inside a foreach loop over Document.Revisions.
common_failure_patterns.cause: Accept/Reject modifies the RevisionCollection while it is being enumerated.
common_failure_patterns.fix: Materialize the collection into a list (e.g., .ToList()) before iterating, or iterate by index.
common_failure_patterns.prevention: Never modify Document.Revisions directly inside a foreach; use a snapshot or index-based loop.

common_failure_patterns.symptom: Compilation or runtime errors arise when calling Document.Protect with ProtectionType.TrackedChanges or mismatched arguments.
common_failure_patterns.cause: The Protect overload was used with an unsupported ProtectionType value or incorrect parameter order.
common_failure_patterns.fix: Use a supported ProtectionType such as ProtectionType.ReadOnly and pass the correct password argument.
common_failure_patterns.prevention: Refer to the Protect method signature in the official documentation and pass only valid enum values.

narrative.overview: The Track Changes category demonstrates how to use Aspose.Words 26.11.0 to create, modify, and manage revision data in Word documents. Verified examples show document creation, enabling revision tracking, performing edits such as paragraph insertion, style changes, table insertion, and then inspecting, accepting, or rejecting the generated revisions.
narrative.purpose: An AI coding agent should generate concise, self-contained C# snippets that employ only the documented Aspose.Words APIs to start and stop revision tracking, perform edits, query the RevisionCollection, and apply accept or reject operations, while always creating any required sample files locally and persisting the final document.
validation_priorities: Confirm that the RevisionCollection contains the exact number and types of revisions expected by the task before proceeding to acceptance or rejection.
maintenance_notes: Periodically review the Aspose.Words release notes to ensure that all example code matches the current revision API surface.
